correctness.rationale: The graph adjacency makes every independent set a subset of one coordinate fiber. Weight equals \(mn-z+d\) (z empty, d double-colored), so attaining the vertex-cover bound forces a full maximum empty fiber and all singleton colors. The rainbow test is equivalent to each color appearing in at least two columns; disjoint inclusion-exclusion for at least three columns gives the displayed formula. The two exceptional products are separately and exhaustively classified as \(C_6\) and \(2K_2\). Independent graph-level brute force for four small instances and matrix/witness tests confirm the boundary calculations, but the proof is general and not based on extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The novelty assessed is the exact classification and number of all minimum functions on the two-factor complete-graph categorical product, not the general vertex-cover lower bound or existing direct-product scalar estimates. The 2022 direct-product primary paper supplies general upper bounds and a clique-product sharpness discussion but no all-optimizer enumeration; the 2020 paper supplies scalar values on cycles and complete multipartite graphs. Actual topic, synonym, and implication searches surfaced no equivalent enumerator. Priority remains conditional on unindexed and partially inaccessible literature.

value.rationale: The exact multiplicity of all minimum functions, together with their complete geometric/colored structure, is a natural refinement of a previously studied graph-product domination problem. The formula covers the entire two-parameter family, distinguishes the two genuinely exceptional dimensions, and gives an explicit exponential asymptotic for fixed smaller factor. Neither the scalar bound nor the generic existence construction determines this count. It can be used to uniformly sample optimal labelings or quantify the density of feasible singleton assignments on minimum vertex covers.
